questions.q: What happens when you run `forge script script/Deploy.s.sol` with no additional flags?
options: It immediately broadcasts the deployment transaction
It simulates the script — no transaction is actually sent
It deletes the existing deployment
It only compiles the script without running it
questions.explain: Without --broadcast, forge script runs a simulation, which is how you catch a broken constructor argument or revert before spending real gas.

questions.q: Why does the lesson recommend `--account` (a keystore account) over a raw `--private-key` flag?
options: Because --private-key is deprecated and no longer works
Because a raw private key in a flag puts a plaintext key into shell history and process arguments — a keystore keeps it encrypted on disk
Because --account is faster to type
Because --private-key only works on testnets
questions.explain: --account uses an encrypted keystore, prompting for a password only at broadcast time, instead of exposing a plaintext key in shell history.

questions.q: What does `foundry.toml`'s `[rpc_endpoints]` table let you do?
options: Deploy to multiple chains simultaneously with one command
Give a full RPC URL a short, reusable alias (like "sepolia") instead of pasting the URL on every command
Automatically verify a contract on Etherscan
Skip the --broadcast flag entirely
questions.explain: [rpc_endpoints] maps short names to full RPC URLs, so --rpc-url sepolia works instead of needing the full URL typed or pasted each time.

questions.q: What does the `--chain` flag actually do when running `forge script`, per this lesson's "real gotcha"?
options: It selects which network the transaction broadcasts to
It only sets the EVM's block.chainid value inside the simulation — it does NOT select the destination network
It has been removed from recent Foundry versions
It automatically funds the deployer account
questions.explain: --chain only affects the simulated chain ID; --rpc-url is what actually controls which network the broadcast transaction is sent to — confusing the two sends a deploy to the wrong network.

questions.q: What can a single `forge script ... --broadcast --verify` command do, as shown in this lesson?
options: Only simulate the deployment, nothing else
Deploy the contract and trigger Etherscan verification in the same command
Only verify an already-deployed contract, without deploying
Automatically generate a .gas-snapshot file
questions.explain: Adding --verify alongside --broadcast and an Etherscan API key lets the deploy script both send the deployment and kick off verification in one step.
